summary: Figure F10_failure_hist illustrates the distribution of failure rates across different keys in a simulated environment. The histogram shows the proportion of attacks that failed, with the mean failure rate being 45.88%. The range of failure rates spans from 0% to 100%, indicating significant variability in attack success across keys.
observations: The mean failure rate is 45.88%, suggesting that slightly more than half of the attacks failed in the simulated environment.
The minimum failure rate is 0%, indicating some keys were completely immune to attacks.
The maximum failure rate is 100%, showing that some keys were entirely vulnerable to attacks.
The first few data points show a range of failure rates from 53.33% to 80.00%, indicating high variability in attack outcomes.
caveats: The data is simulated and not based on real-world experiments, so the results should not be interpreted as empirical findings.
The Hoeffding bound requires that the failure rate $ p(x) < 0.5 $, but the data includes values above this threshold, which may affect the validity of certain statistical inferences.
